source: design 0007 (Frames): every outcome is the design's, written by hand in vectors/generator/streams.js; no reference implementation exists yet

formats.body_bytes: Byte k of stream id's body is ((id mod 251) + (k mod 251)) mod 251, with k counted from the body's start.
formats.bytes: A list of parts, concatenated: {"hex": "<lowercase hex>"} or {"fill": [byte, count]}.
formats.frames: Decoding. `side` is the decoder: "receiver" (main, after a handshake that granted stream), "sender" (the service, likewise) or "core" (a freedom-cored connection, which never grants stream). `input` is fed whole, and in any chunking the outcome is the same. `expect.frames` lists every frame decoded, as ["json", text], ["data", id, bytes], ["end", id], ["abort", id, code, message] or ["credit", id, n]. `expect.truncated` means the input stops inside a frame: EOF there truncates it. `expect.error` is the first failure's category, from the header check, the ID or the payload; frames before it are not asserted.
formats.encodings: `frame` encodes to exactly `hex`, or is refused with `error` and nothing written. `frame` is as in `frames`.
formats.sender: The service's side. Steps run in order. A step with `do` is an action with its `expect`ed result: ["request", id] main's request (ok, or a protocol error); ["cancel", id] main's cancel ("cancelled": the reply or abort is queued and the work is to stop; "late": nothing changes); ["credit", id, n] main's credit frame ("taken" into the stream's account, "late" for a stream that has ended, or a protocol error); ["head", id, body] the response that heads request id, opening a stream if body is true; ["reply", id] the request's one reply without a body (an error, or a result); ["push", id, n] the producer offers its next n body bytes (`taken` says how many were queued; the producer keeps the rest); ["finish", id] the end, after every byte queued; ["abort", id, code]. Producer refusals are `refused`: gone, unknown, answered, not_open, ended, too_large or closed. A step with `write` takes frames from the writer until it has none, and they must be exactly those listed; `write_some` takes exactly those listed and may leave more. Written frames are ["head", id], ["reply", id], ["cancelled", id] (the reply a cancel made the request's only one), ["data", id, offset, length] (bytes of the body from offset), ["end", id] and ["abort", id, code]. `check` compares the writer's held bytes (queued body bytes across streams) and, per ID, whether the request is live, its producer's room (the window's room within the writer's, null without a body that takes bytes) and its queued bytes (null without a body). A push takes as much as the room allows, except that one the writer's cap would cut below 4 KiB takes nothing. `repeat` runs its step that many times. `config.data_cap` replaces the writer's 16 MiB cap. After a protocol error, every main step reports the same error, every producer step is refused with `closed`, and nothing is written.
formats.receiver: Main's side. ["request", id] main sends request id (ok, or request_order for main's own bug); ["reply", id, opens] its reply arrives, a head with body: true when opens ("deliver", "retired", or a protocol error); ["data", id, n] a data frame with the service's next n bytes of stream id; ["end", id]; ["abort", id, code]. Frames give "data", "end" (bytes are left to pull), "end_drained" (nothing is left: the record and ring are gone), "abort", "dropped" (the stream is retiring), or a protocol error. ["pull", id, max] the consumer pulls: null without a record, else the chunk as [offset, length] of the body, the credit to send (null for none) and whether it is the last. ["cancel", id] a local cancel: "send_cancel", "freed" (end had arrived: nothing is sent) or "nothing". `check` compares, per ID, the record (null for none) with its state (pending, retired_pending, open, eof, retiring), whether its ring is allocated, the bytes in it, and received and returned bytes; and the outstanding records. After a protocol error, every frame and reply reports the same error.
